answer: Before an agent can influence a market vote, it must lock a scarce, slashable deposit for a fixed period, with one deposit buying only one vote. If it is caught coordinating fake identities, a randomly selected set of its votes is challenged; failure to provide valid, distinct proofs of control burns the deposit and removes those votes. The ember, jade, and sable agents may all participate, but multiplying names does not multiply voting weight: an attacker must tie up real capital per identity and risks losing it, making a large Sybil campaign costly rather than free.
